stage1.impression: A dead-frontal, evenly lit elevation of a shopfront, with flat grey stucco, clean CG roller shutters and an upper bay lit as brightly as the bar, so it reads as dusk or an overcast day rather than night. The room behind the glass is warm but soft and mostly hidden behind the fluted lower panel. The frosted lightbox with the dancer is the one strong idea, but the pale blue EARF letters read as vinyl signage and no tinted speaker is visible, so the frame has no hero colour. It looks like an architectural visualisation elevation, not a magazine night photograph.

blocking_9: Night hierarchy: the shopfront glow must be clearly the brightest thing, with the upper facade and neighbours falling to deep but detailed shadow (upper facade lum_median about 20 to 35, against a lit window of about 70 to 100)
One saturated colour: an Ember speaker or its red light must be legible through the glass (now none in frame)
The glass must behave like glass at night: faint reflections of the street lamps and of the opposite street, and a slight sheen, rather than perfectly transparent panes
The upper building and neighbours need real-world weathering (grime under sills, paint sheen variation, stains, cables or a downpipe) instead of clean CG surfaces and banded shutters
A believable photographer's viewpoint with a little street (kerb, wet or worn pavement, a pool of lamp light) and some sign of life in the window
Full-resolution render without denoiser softness inside the room

defects.what: The upper bay and siding are lit flat and as bright as the shop interior (median 95.3 vs 97.3), so it reads as day or dusk, not night
The roller shutters are clean CG slats with soft blotchy shading and regular banding, with no grime or wear
The bay's base and cornice are a smooth untextured grey extrusion, with no paint wear or dirt line
The frosted EARF letters are the brightest object outside the lamp (median 194), cold blue (R188 G195 B201) against a warm room, and read as applied vinyl signage
The lightbox is a neutral grey-white (R130 G127 B130) with no warmth and no visible thickness or edge glow; it reads as a flat printed panel
The fluted lower panel blocks most of the room; the clear panes show the room only as a soft, featureless warm blur
The glass carries no reflections of the street lamps or the street behind the camera
The pendant lamp clips (6.7 % of a small patch), acceptable as a practical but hard-edged
The neighbour's upper window is a pure black void (crush 16.7 % in the left strip), with no glass, curtain or reflection
The neighbour's left shutter repeats the same CG slat texture
The right neighbour is a blank, evenly lit stucco plane with no detail
There is almost no pavement: a 15 px strip, so the building floats with no street
A perfectly frontal, level elevation with an even flat light reads as an architectural drawing render, not a photograph; no colour anywhere but the warm interior

changes.problem: The street lamps flood the whole facade evenly, so the upper building is as bright as the lit room and the frame reads as day or dusk.

evidence.measured: upper facade lum_median 95.3; window interior lum_median 97.3; vertical profile bins 95, 95, 83, 39, 46, 80, 69, 25

change.from: 260.0 W, 3400 K, lighting the facade evenly
change.to: one or two lamps at 60 to 90 W, 3000 K, placed at kerb height off to one side so they make a pool on the pavement and a falloff up the facade, with the third removed

changes.expected: The upper facade drops to deep, warm-grey shadow with its detail just held; the shopfront becomes the brightest thing in the frame

changes.problem: The frame is overexposed for a night street.

change.to: 1.6 to 1.8 after c1, set so the room's clear panes keep a median of about 70 to 90

changes.expected: A frame median of about 35 to 45, with the window glow holding and the facade in shadow

changes.problem: No EARF speaker is visible, so the frame has no hero and no saturated colour, and the dead-frontal elevation reads as a drawing.

evidence.measured: the clear panes show only a warm blur (R121 G91 B69); no red anywhere in the frame

change.to: position about [-8.0, 1.0, 1.55], 3 to 4 m to the right of centre, turned so the sightline through the right-hand clear pane (or the open door) lands on an Ember speaker and its lamps in the listening room; 40 mm; verticals kept true with shift, not tilt; bring in 1 to 1.5 m of pavement and kerb at the bottom and crop the bay to its lower half

changes.expected: A slight three-quarter view with depth in the reveals and the steel frame, a red Ember glow readable through the glass as the one saturated note, and the street grounding the building

changes.problem: The frosted EARF name is the brightest and coldest object on the shopfront and reads as vinyl signage.

evidence.measured: lum_median 194, R188 G195 B201 (blue-shifted) against the room's R121 G91 B69

change.setting: the window's frosted name emission; render.white_balance_k
change.to: 0.08 to 0.12 so it is lit mostly from the room behind; 3600 to 3800 K so the neutrals stop going blue

changes.expected: The letters read as etched frost catching the room's warm light, a little brighter than the glass behind them, not white

changes.problem: The lightbox is a flat, cold grey-white panel that reads as a print rather than thick frosted acrylic glowing from behind.

evidence.measured: lum_median 127.9, R130 G127 B130 (neutral to violet), range 102; edge step 1 px with no glow at its border

change.setting: the screens' images emission; frosted acrylic roughness
change.to: 0.55 to 0.6, and make the frosted face slightly less rough so the image's soft gradient shows; let the polished edge of the panel catch light (a 1 to 2 px bright rim)

changes.expected: The panel glows a little less than the letters did, with an even soft falloff and a visible lit edge, like thick acrylic in a reveal

changes.problem: The shopfront glass is perfectly transparent, which no glass is at night from across a lit street.

evidence.measured: no reflected highlights; the clear panes' p95 of 196 comes from the interior only

change.to: real glass (IOR 1.5) with faint reflections of the street lamps and the opposite facade, plus a very slight smudge or dust roughness map at 2 to 5 % strength

changes.expected: One or two soft lamp reflections and ghosted street shapes across the panes, which sell the glass as a real surface

changes.problem: The upper building and its neighbours are smooth CG surfaces with no weathering.

evidence.measured: the cornice and bay base are a near-uniform grey (range 121 only because of the shadow line), with no texture at 2x

change.setting: the finish of the facade and neighbours
change.from: clean paint and stucco, CG slat shutters
change.to: old repainted siding with sheen variation, a dirt line under the sills and the cornice, a downpipe, a few cables and a meter box; a curtain or a dim lamp in the neighbour's black window

changes.expected: The building reads as an ordinary weathered San Francisco storefront; the black void at the top left gets detail

changes.problem: There is no sign of life in the window, and the clear panes show a blur.

evidence.measured: lum_range 150, but no recognisable objects at 3x

change.from: props deep in the room only
change.to: a lit candle in an amber votive, two rocks glasses and a folded menu on the sill or counter just inside the clear panes, and a coat on a hook by the door; haze 0.035 up to 0.05 so the pendant beams read through the glass

changes.expected: Small warm highlights and recognisable objects in the near plane of the window; the frame reads as a bar open tonight

out_of_scope.request: Lower or open the fluted panel across the bottom of the shopfront glass so more of the room shows
out_of_scope.why: It is part of the shopfront's design, which the card fixes

out_of_scope.request: Put an Ember speaker (or the Fog pair) in the window itself so the hero is visible from the street
out_of_scope.why: The room's layout is fixed; only the camera can bring a speaker into view (c3)
